title: OrbitLink partnership play journal
body:
Context:
Quick scratch for OrbitLink Health — mid-market digital health platform (claimed 120M ARR in slide deck, ~220 eng/ops users). Contact discovered via intro: Sasha Mironov (Head of Platform). They are exploring in-product conversational features and clinician-assist summarization.

Why this matters (hypothesis):
- High token volumes (notes, transcripts) + strict latency needs for clinician flow -> fits Redwood value prop (dedicated pools + latency SLOs).
- Regulated data: likely wants private deployment or VPC. Good upsell path: start Hosted for PoC then fast migrate to Private.
- Comp set: Anthropic/OpenAI for prototyping; Vector DB vendors + managed inference partners (Run:ai/Replicate) for on-prem. Our differentiation: predictable token economics + rollout/rollback tooling for quality.

Quick account research (raw):
- HQ: Boston; funding: Series B (2023); customers: 40 health systems (self-reported); stack hints: heavy GCP, Postgres, uses Amazon Transcribe for calls, experiments with Weaviate for retrieval.
- Regulatory posture: SOC2 + HIPAA BAAs in contract pages.
- Product roadmap (public/PRs): clinician summarization Q3, patient Q4, EHR connectors planned.
- Org signals: hiring ML infra and platform SRE roles -> runway to adopt dedicated infra.

Primary contacts (gathered):
- Sasha Mironov — Head of Platform (sasha@orbitlink.health) — exec sponsor candidate
- Leila Gomez — Lead ML Eng (leila@...), GitHub: leilagomez
- Dr. Evan Park — Clinical product owner (evan@) — cares about accuracy/latency
- Sales/Procurement TBD after initial scoping
(Confirm emails via LinkedIn prior to outreach)

Outbound sequence (6 touches, conservative):
- Day 0: Short intro email from Asha (1-2 lines + one pager PDF link). CTA: 20–30 min scoping call.
- Day 3: Follow-up — include a quick token economics sketch (estimated tokens/day x 30d cost delta vs self-host). Attach sample latency SLO graph.
- Day 8: Leverage Sashas' hire (platform) — send a technical note: "how Redwood handles KV cache and clinician session consistency" (1 page).
- Day 14: Anecdote-based social proof: short case study (healthcare) + ask for internal tech review.
- Day 21: LinkedIn + slack nudge (if workspace overlap) + offer 6-week pilot with data residency and KMS options.
- Day 35: Break glass: CEO note offering direct intro to our product lead for high-touch pilot setup.

Cold email draft (v0 — very short):
Subject: Low-friction pilot for OrbitLink clinician summaries
Hi Sasha —
I’m Asha on the partnerships team at Redwood Inference. We help healthcare platforms run low-latency, cost-predictable LLM inference (hosted -> private) with built-in rollout and quality guards.
Quick ask: would you take 20 minutes next week to see a 6-week pilot plan scoped to OrbitLink notes/transcripts? I can share an example cost/latency estimate for your average 1k token session.
Thanks,
Asha

Follow-up variant with value proof (v0):
Sasha —
Attached: 30s snapshot of how one medtech customer reduced per-interaction inference cost by 2.6x using dedicated pools + caching. If you want, I’ll draft the same estimate for OrbitLink using three sample transcripts.

Objection handling cheatsheet (common responses and play):
- "We run everything in-house / won't hand PII to external vendors" -> Play: Offer VPC/on-prem pilot + KMS/HSM integration + BAA. Emphasize private control plane.
- "We already have a self-hosted inference team" -> Play: Differentiate on SLOs + ops effort. Ask for their TCO (infra + on-call + SRE time) and compare with Redwood dedicated pool pricing. Offer a small benchmark (our runtime vs their baseline) on a realistic prompt set.
- "Latency too high for clinician flow" -> Play: Show previous 95th percentile numbers, propose canary to validate at-mock load, explain caching for repeated context.
- "Cost too unpredictable" -> Play: Committed capacity + token forecasting dashboard + Optimize recommendations.

Technical hooks to emphasize in technical outreach:
- Retrieval-augmented generation: integration patterns (RAG with per-user KV cache, prefix caching for clinician templates).
- Native streaming + function calling (for structured results/summaries).
- Quantization & model selection: how we route to cheaper quantized variants for low-criticality tasks.
- Rollouts: canary + auto-fallback to smaller model on error to keep UI responsive.

Pilot proposal (6 weeks, minimal):
- Week 0: Align scope + NDA/BAA + sample transcript delivery (we give template).
- Week 1: Integration spike (1 engineer each) — connect ingest -> Redwood hosted endpoint (or private eval infra).
- Week 2–3: Run parallel inference (compare existing infra vs Redwood) on sample set: latency, cost, quality.
- Week 4: Iterate prompt + model selection; optimize batch/caching settings.
- Week 5: Run clinician UAT on 50–100 sessions; collect accuracy/regression signals.
- Week 6: Deliver TCO + migration plan + optional Dedicated/Private quote.
Deliverables: latency/cost dashboard, regression report on prompt set, migration checklist.

Quick numbers (back-of-envelope to include in follow up):
- Estimated active sessions/day (conservative): 4k sessions/day x 1k tokens average -> 4M tokens/day -> 120M tokens/month.
- Hosted cost @ baseline model: ~$0.12 / 1k tokens -> $14.4k/month. Dedicated expected unit cost (after pooling): ~$0.045 / 1k tokens -> $5.4k/month. Delta ~9k/mo -> pitch savings + reliability. (Flag: need real sampling from OrbitLink to refine.)

Risk/Questions to resolve (notes to self):
- Need real transcript samples (PII scrubbed) to benchmark; request via secure upload link only.
- Confirm whether OrbitLink requires on-prem air-gapped for any pilot customers.
- Double-check procurement lead time for HIPAA BAA and legal sign-off window (enterprise sales calendar).
- Who owns SSO / identity (Okta?) — affects onboarding time.

Competitive intel (quick):
- Anthropic: strong model Evals; lacks dedicated private product that integrates rollout tooling (check recent roadmap).
- OpenAI: simple dev speed; lacks private deployment at scale (for now) and more expensive at high token volumes.
- Run:ai/Replicate etc: strong at self-host orchestration but not a full managed inference runtime + developer API.

Next actions (owners & dates):
- 2025-02-15: Send v1 intro email + attach 1-pager (owner: Asha).
- 2025-02-18: If no reply, send token-econ sketch (owner: Marco).
- 2025-02-25: Technical note to Leila about KV cache pattern + sample latency profile (owner: Talia).
- 2025-03-04: Prep pilot contract template (legal checklist) for quick turn (owner: partnerships-ops).

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- Build a 1-click sample generator for prospects: drop 3 transcripts -> show cost/latency delta + recommended rollout plan. Could shorten decision time.
- If OrbitLink asks for on-prem benchmark, propose limited scoped lab: 1 quantized model, 1 GPU node, 24h synthetic load test.

Unresolved:
- Confirm exact tokenization assumptions for their transcript format (are timestamps stored inline? that impacts token count).
- Do they compress/normalize clinician notes server-side? (affects retrieval size)

End notes: keep outreach conversational and remove heavy-sell numbers until I get their sample data. This doc = working brain dump. Will iterate email templates after call recording and sample transcripts arrive.
